$comment: Acceptance criteria for issue 189. policies/high-assurance.json escalates four reasons to blocking; engine/completion.py never reads the profile, so escalate_to_blocking is unreachable from that module and every profile behaves as GOVERNOR_LITE. Verified before this bar was written: vocabulary.classify('NO_CRITERIA_DECLARED','GOVERNOR_HIGH_ASSURANCE') returns blocking=True, while completion.py:239 sets "blocking": False as a literal and returns before any classification, and the three _classify calls at :175, :209 and :259 omit the profile argument so the GOVERNOR_LITE default is always taken. engine/retirement.py:68 does it correctly -- V.classify(u['reason'], m['condition']['profile']) -- which is what makes this a defect rather than a deliberate asymmetry. THE VACUITY THIS BAR IS BUILT AGAINST: fixing only the :239 path. Four reasons are escalated by high-assurance and three call sites take the default; a bar that checks NO_CRITERIA_DECLARED alone would go green with ACCEPTANCE_UNSTATED, NON_GOALS_UNSTATED and NO_ACCEPTED_DECISIONS still inert. C5 exists for that. It was AMENDED during the work -- see its own comment -- and C5's original draft was vacuous -- it called vocabulary.classify directly, which already works, so it went green against the unfixed engine; running it is what found that. NOTE C2 IS AN EXISTING ASSERTION, NOT A NEW ONE: conformance/acceptance.py:73 currently asserts a missing bar is non-blocking, unconditionally. That assertion partly encodes the bug. It must gain a profile dimension and keep passing for GOVERNOR_LITE -- absence of a bar genuinely does not stop work at LITE, and a fix that makes everything block everywhere is a different defect wearing this issue's number. WHY THE ASSERTIONS AND NOT ONLY THIS BAR: a bar stops being consulted the moment the issue closes; conformance/acceptance.py runs forever.

criteria.$comment: C1 THE DEFECT. A barless authority under GOVERNOR_HIGH_ASSURANCE must read blocking. Red today: the literal at completion.py:239 makes it False at every profile.
C2 THE CONTROL, and it is an EXISTING assertion that must survive. At GOVERNOR_LITE a missing bar is non-blocking and must stay so. A fix that blocks at every profile satisfies C1 and is wrong.
criteria.target: bash -c 'python3 conformance/acceptance.py | grep -q "\[PASS\] and it is non-blocking (absence of a bar does not stop work)"'

criteria.$comment: C3 NO CALL SITE TAKES THE DEFAULT. Structural, in the spirit of conformance/imports.py: _classify must never be called with one argument, or the defect returns silently the next time a site is added.
C4 THE LITERAL IS GONE. completion.py must not hardcode a blocking verdict for a reason the vocabulary classifies.

C5 AMENDED DURING THE WORK, and the amendment is recorded rather than quietly made. AS DECLARED it required the four escalated reason names to appear literally in conformance/acceptance.py. That is TEXT PRESENCE: a comment listing the names satisfies it, which is this repository's oldest defect wearing another hat -- imports.py refusing to grep source for imports, SUPERSEDED_RE matching prose about supersession. It would also have hardcoded a second copy of policies/high-assurance.json into the suite. AS AMENDED it derives the reasons from the policy file and asserts each one actually escalates at GOVERNOR_HIGH_ASSURANCE and does not at GOVERNOR_LITE. DEMONSTRATED STRONGER, not asserted: neutering vocabulary._load_profiles so the policy packs are ignored fails this criterion and the HIGH_ASSURANCE check, while a file that merely contains the four names would satisfy the literal version unchanged. Note the amendment LOOSENS the letter and TIGHTENS the behaviour, which is the direction that needs a record: nothing but this note distinguishes a legitimate correction from a convenient one.
criteria.target: bash -c 'python3 conformance/acceptance.py | grep -q "\[PASS\] every escalated reason blocks at HIGH_ASSURANCE and not at LITE"'

criteria.$comment: C6 FLOOR CONTROL for C5. An empty escalate_to_blocking list makes the loop above run zero times and pass having established nothing -- all([]) is True, the vacuous-truth shape this repository keeps shipping.
criteria.target: bash -c 'python3 conformance/acceptance.py | grep -qE "\[PASS\] the escalation policy was read \([1-9]"'

criteria.$comment: C7 THE SECOND ROUTE. Two paths reach NO_CRITERIA_DECLARED: the adapter refuses an empty array and the engine classifies its unknown, or an adapter SERVES one and completion.py raises the reason itself. Only the second line carried the hardcoded blocking value. THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS TEST COVERED ONLY THE FIRST ROUTE, and restoring the literal left every assertion green -- the mutation did not fire, because the real adapter never takes that path. C4's structural check that no literal remains is not the same as a test that the branch behaves, and this repository has shipped that gap before. Found by mutating rather than by reading.
criteria.target: bash -c 'python3 conformance/acceptance.py | grep -q "\[PASS\] the engine.s own branch blocks under GOVERNOR_HIGH_ASSURANCE"'

criteria.$comment: C8 CONTROL for C7, and the guard that makes it non-vacuous: the same branch must NOT block at LITE, and the stub's guard must still be removable or the two checks above run against an adapter that refuses anyway.
criteria.target: bash -c 'python3 conformance/acceptance.py | grep -q "\[PASS\] the guard is still removable for the profile route"'
